previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a severe frontal headache, fever, and elevated white blood cell count. The headache responded well to Imitrex, supporting a diagnosis of migraine, though initial concern for meningitis led to empiric antibiotics, later discontinued. She was found to have cellulitis in the left lower leg and a urinary tract infection caused by E. coli, both treated with appropriate antibiotics. Her INR was elevated on admission, so Coumadin was held and later restarted at discharge. HIV medications were resumed, and she was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor INR, and follow up on pending lab results.

consistent with prior.
